episodes.211360: An upper level trough and low level trough to the northwest of Hawaii brought numerous flooding impacts. These flooding impacts closed roads and damaged property across the state.
episodes.212444: An isolated waterspout developed in association with a well-developed convective cloud line over the oceanside of the lower Florida Keys.
episodes.212778: Mid- to upper-level short wave troughs, a jet streak near the region and above normal moisture being steered from the Caribbean resulted in moist and unstable conditions. Available moisture, diurnal heating, local sea breeze convergence, and orographic |effects all also aided in afternoon showers and t-storms. These resulted in Rio Blanco and Rio Grande rising out of their banks and resulting in River Flooding.

events.narrative: Naguabo Emergency Manager reported that Rio Blanco is out of its banks. The Intersection of PR-191 and PR-31, near the highway exit, was closed due to impassibility.

Emergency managers reported flooding affecting PR-956 and PR-186 in Sector Galateo Barrio Bartolo due to the Rio Grande overflowing its banks. The roads are impassable, and local officials have proceeded to close them to the public.

Heavy rain developed over the eastern slopes of Maui.  Emergency management and the local news reported multiple impacts. Hawaii News Now reported Hana High & Elementary School was temporarily closed on Tuesday April 7 due to flooding. The Department of Education said some classrooms had water damage. Water was also reported on Hana Highway.
